text: Normalize connection-size force without slowing small-aim layout convergence
description: Fix the regression introduced when hierarchy force changed from a 0.5–1.0 share weight to absolute flowValue*5 with a 0.02 floor. Absolute graph value scale should not determine convergence speed. Normalize positive transported flow against a robust reference across visible connections, compress extreme ratios, and retain a meaningful minimum force. Keep inverse-surface endpoint movement so smaller aims move more than larger aims. Verify relative strength, scale invariance, zero-flow fallback, and surface movement with focused tests.

status.comment: Normalized force weighting and focused verification are complete; awaiting Felix's visual acceptance in the existing runtime.

reflection: Confirmed regression from commit history: hierarchy force previously used 0.5+0.5*share, then changed to clamp(flowValue*5, 0.02, 1.5), causing many small-flow connections to receive ~0.02 rather than the former 0.5–1.0 and settle roughly 25× more slowly. Implemented median-relative visible-flow normalization with square-root compression and 0.5–1.5 bounds; a median connection is 0.75. Preserved inverse-surface endpoint movement. This is invariant to absolute graph value scale and computed only when graph links update, not every animation frame. Verification: graph-forces tests 7/7 pass; frontend vue-tsc passes.
